prerequisites: Having previously passed Machine Design and Kinematics and Dynamics of Machines courses, or at least being familiar with the basic concepts explained in them.

learning_outcomes.text: Comprehensively apply the fundamentals of structural systems, elasticity, strength of materials, thermal engineering, machine design, kinematics and dynamics of mechanisms, hydraulic machines, as well as fundamental graphical concepts for professional development in mechanical engineering.
Solve problems posed by the analysis of deformable solids, structural systems, and machine design through qualitative and quantitative analysis, hypothesis formulation, and solution proposal.

Produce written and oral works and reports: adequately express theoretical knowledge, resolution methods, results, and aspects related to deformable solid equilibrium, structural systems, and machine design using specific vocabulary, forms of representation, and terminology.
Formulate ideas, debate, and make decisions in group work within the disciplines of mechanical engineering.

Develop designs and projects in the field of industrial constructions and machine design, as well as perform measurements, calculations, studies, reports, and other similar tasks, related to problematic situations that may arise in the field of the specialty.
Apply mandatory legislation, specifications, regulations, and standards in the field of mechanical engineering.

syllabus_topics: Basic concepts of the Finite Element Method (FEM) in linear static analysis
Introduction to modal analysis using FEM
Introduction to fatigue analysis using FEM
teaching_methods: Computer labs (mechanical analysis of parts with finite element software)
assessment_rules: The final grade is based on a written exam (50%) and team project work (50%). A minimum attendance of 75% of the contact hours is required. Both parts must be passed separately in the ordinary call; a passed part's grade carries over to the extraordinary call. The extraordinary call will consist of exams for the failed parts, or a single final exam covering all parts for 100% of the grade.
